1.explanation:
1. OrderedList/OrderedList.mdx — shows how the <ol class=“bx--list--ordered”> markup is rendered in the docs and what the expected native decimal style should look like.
2. UnorderedList/UnorderedList.mdx — demonstrates nested-list behavior and how nested lists opt out of the custom counter (via .bx--list--nested).
3. node_modules/carbon-components/scss/components/list/_list.scss — the core SCSS where .bx--list--ordered:not(.bx--list--nested) { counter-reset: item; } and li::before { counter-increment: item; content: counter(item) "."; } live; removing this rule fixes the Firefox start-at-zero bug.
4. packages/components-react/src/components/OrderedList/OrderedList.js — the React wrapper that applies the bx--list--ordered class, responsible for passing the right props and className into the DOM <ol>.
5. packages/gatsby-theme-carbon/src/components/markdown/Markdown.module.scss — in the Gatsby theme this module adds an extra scope (.Markdown-module--list) on top of bx--list classes and showcases why merely overriding counter-reset in user CSS is being out-scoped by Carbon’s built-in specificity.
1.bug_scenario:
The issue surfaces in Firefox when using the built-in Carbon ordered-list styles.  By default Carbon disables the native “decimal” numbering and instead applies its own counter via:

•  counter-reset: item on the <ol class=“bx--list--ordered:not(.bx--list--nested)”>
•  li::before { content: counter(item) "."; counter-increment: item; }

In Firefox that custom counter isn’t resetting cleanly between separate lists (or nested levels), so your first item can start at “7” (or any leftover count) rather than “1.”  Attempts to override counter-reset on the <ol> via inline or external CSS don’t win because the Carbon selector is more specific.  The only surefire workaround is removing the counter-reset rule entirely from Carbon’s SCSS.
